llm.summary: The skill is mostly coherent for WeChat article/account retrieval, but it stores WeChat backend login sessions in plaintext and can fetch arbitrary URLs, so it should be reviewed before installation.

dimensions.detail: The skill needs network access for WeChat and local browser fallback, but the main article path accepts any URL and Playwright can navigate to it without origin allowlisting.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No separate installer, dependency installer, remote payload fetch, tool wrapper, service, or startup hook was found; the package consists of markdown, Python scripts, and a small account cache.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Most operations are user-directed CLI actions, but article fetching does not enforce WeChat-only URLs and CURRENT_TASK asks a future agent to read memory files outside the skill scope.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It persists cookies/tokens, QR login state, QR images, and account cache files under scripts/cache or a caller-supplied session path without encryption, owner-only permissions, expiry, cleanup, or symlink/path hardening.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Article extraction, account search, article listing, and WeChat MP session management are disclosed in the skill body and usage docs, but the authenticated backend capability gives reusable account-session authority beyond simple public article reading.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable letting the skill use a WeChat MP backend session, including QR login and cookie/token reuse. Use it in an isolated workspace, do not commit or share scripts/cache/session files, pass only real https://mp.weixin.qq.com article URLs, and avoid following the external memory-file checklist unless you explicitly intend to expose that context.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Session management and QR login are disclosed in SKILL.md and usage.md, so the claimed hidden-purpose mismatch is downgraded; the remaining issue is underprotected credential persistence.
[AE1] expected: The referenced scripts are present in the artifact and were inspected, so the incomplete-inspection concern is not supported in this final review.
[SDI-1] expected: QR login and backend session capture fit the documented account-search and article-listing workflow, but they are high-impact and need stronger user-facing controls.
[SDI-2] expected: Reusing saved cookies/tokens is part of the stated session feature, but saving reusable credentials in plaintext materially increases account-session exposure risk.
[AS3] unexpected: The CURRENT_TASK resume checklist asks to read external memory files; that is not needed for WeChat article retrieval and should be removed or require explicit user approval.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill lacks explicit permission boundaries for network, browser, filesystem, and credential access; this matters because the capability surface is broader than public article fetching.
[SQP-2] expected: Local session and cache writes are documented, but the docs and code do not clearly warn that stored cookie/token values are sensitive account credentials.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese UI text and zh_CN parameters are expected for a WeChat MP integration and are not treated as a security concern here.
[T09] unexpected: The SSRF-style concern is supported: the article CLI accepts an arbitrary URL and both requests and Playwright fetch it without validating scheme, host, redirects, or private-network destinations.
[T09] expected: The plaintext credential-storage concern is supported: session_store.py writes cookie and token JSON with normal file-write semantics and qr_login.py stores login state without cleanup or file permission hardening.
[T05] unexpected: The cross-scope memory-read instruction in CURRENT_TASK is unnecessary for the skill's purpose, although no artifact showed memory modification or exfiltration.
